newsitem.title: USA: Police release sketch of Cosby murder suspect.
newsitem.headline: Police release sketch of Cosby murder suspect.

text.p: Los Angeles police released a composite sketch on Saturday of the man suspected of killing Ennis Cosby, the 27-year-old son of entertainer Bill Cosby.
According to the sketch, the suspect is a white male, 25 to 32 years old, of average height and weight. Police said he was wearing a light-coloured knit cap.

Contrary to earlier speculation, Police Cmdr. Tim McBride said the suspect was on foot, rather than following Cosby in a car. He said police still believed robbery was the most probable motive for the attack.
Police also released a sketch of a second white male, believed to be a witness, who was described as in his late 20's to early 30's with dark hair, a moustache and a goatee.
McBride told a news conference the witness may have been driving by when Cosby was murdered early on Thursday as he stopped to change a flat tire on a California freeway.
"This individual is not a suspect and detectives are seeking him as a potential witness at this time," McBride said.
He said the witness was driving a blue hatchback with a license plate number thought to be GRH921. He said the license plate may have been from out of state.
The sketch is the first big development in the case since the murder took place in the fashionable community of Bel Air.

Investigators had hoped to release a sketch of the killer on Friday but that was delayed in order to give their key witness, a woman who saw part of the murder, more time to get over the shock of the attack and the crush of media attention.
During the news conference, McBride urged reporters once again to respect the woman's privacy.
"This is a long road to the end of the criminal justice system and it's important these people be available to testify and they not be frightened off," he said.
Some television stations broadcast pictures of the woman, described as a 47-year-old screenwriter, standing near the crime scene wearing a short skirt and a fur coat and talking to police.
McBride declined to confirm reports Cosby called the woman on his cellular phone to come to his aid when he pulled off the road to change his tire.
Cosby's death has sparked an outpouring of support from politicians and friends of Cosby family.
In San Francisco, Martin Luther King III, son of the slain civil rights leader, called the murder a tragedy.

"When I was a small child, Bill Cosby came to my home to comfort my brother and I when my father was gunned down. And to see almost 30 years later his son being gunned down, it's very tragic," he said.

"He represents so much for so many. He did so much in terms of television and getting people to understand there is black family life -- all black families do not have separate households -- a positive image. That's why my prayers go out for his family," King said.
Bill Cosby played a physician and head of a family in the long-running "Cosby Show" on NBC during the 1980s. His current series, "Cosby", appears on CBS.
McBride said investigators were following up on a number of leads, interviewing potential witnesses and listening to tapes of 911 emergency calls to determine who killed Cosby.
"Obviously this is a critical case, we are doing everything we can," he said. "We have a lot of leads."
